newsitem.title: CHINA: China rejects appeal of jailed dissident.
newsitem.headline: China rejects appeal of jailed dissident.

text.p: A Chinese court has rejected the appeal of dissident Liu Nianchun against what he said was illegal incarceration, his wife said on Tuesday.

Beijing's Chaoyang District Court rejected Liu's appeal on Monday on the grounds that a petition he initiated in 1995 "contained attacks against the people's government", said a copy of the verdict seen by Reuters.
The petition "exceeded the limits of the constitution and the law", the verdict said.
Liu had argued that the constitution guaranteed his right to freedom of speech.
His wife, Chu Hailan, said by telephone she would appeal. She has 15 days in which to do so.

The 48-year-old dissident was ordered last July to serve three years of re-education through labour at a camp in the northeastern province of Heilongjiang. Re-education through labour is an administrative punishment that can be imposed by the authorities without recourse to prosecutors or the courts.
